headline: SMCI Q4 FY26 blowout: rev $11.1B (+93% Y/Y), GM doubles to 17.5%, Q1 FY27 guide $14.5-15.5B (vs $11.8B consensus); FY27 outlook up to $72B; backlog record with $60B new orders in Q4; +23% pre-market
summary: Super Micro (SMCI) reported unaudited Q4 FY26 (June qtr) after the bell Aug 11: net sales $11.12B vs $10.2B prior qtr and $5.8B Q4'25 (+93% Y/Y), net income $1.178B vs $195M year-ago, diluted EPS $1.62 vs $0.31, non-GAAP EPS $1.70. Gross margin expanded to 17.5% from 9.9% Q3 and 9.5% Q4'25 — the doubling was the biggest positive surprise vs consensus for a low-margin server assembler. Company guided FY27 revenue as high as $72B (vs FY26 actual ~$39B implied) and Q1 FY27 revenue $14.5-15.5B (midpoint 27% above $11.82B consensus). Backlog at record; >$60B in new orders received during Q4 alone. Stock +23% pre-market to ~$55.91. Loop Capital hiked PT $50→$70 (Buy); Wedbush raised $34→$40 (Neutral). Read-through: (1) validates the AI-server ODM demand curve is re-accelerating rather than digesting Blackwell backlog, (2) big positive setup for NVDA/AMD/MU pre-earnings — SMCI shipments are the demand signal for GB200/GB300 platform ramps, (3) rehabilitates the SMCI-specific narrative that lost 30%+ of value over the past year on 10-K delays and margin compression — this print resolves both. Watch: sustainability of 17.5% GM given SMCI's mix shift toward liquid-cooled full-rack systems where component cost pass-through is higher.

headline: CoreWeave Q2 beat: rev $2.58B (+112% Y/Y), backlog $104B (excl >$25B Q3 commitments), Q3 guide $3.4-3.6B (~158% growth); Meta expanded to ~$21B, Anthropic multi-year, Jane Street $6B; 2026 capex $30B+; CRWV +15-18% AH
summary: CoreWeave (CRWV) reported Q2 2026 after the bell Aug 11: revenue $2.575B vs $2.56B consensus (+112% Y/Y, +24% Q/Q), adjusted operating income $128M (margins expanding sequentially, expected to continue through 2H). Net loss widened to $626M from $290M year-ago driven by depreciation on the accelerated buildout. Revenue backlog $104B — a step-function up — and management explicitly excluded >$25B in fresh Q3 commitments from that figure. Active power 1.5 GW. Q3 revenue guide $3.4-3.6B implies ~158% growth at midpoint. Named contract wins in Q2: Meta expanded to ~$21B AI-cloud capacity through Dec 2032, Anthropic multi-year (already-announced Apr 2026 Claude deal expanded), Jane Street $6B (first material non-hyperscaler AI-cloud tenant). Full-year 2026 capex guided to at least $30B — more than double 2025 spend. Stock +14.79% AH to $103.68 (reports show +18% pre-mkt intraday). Read-through: (1) removes the near-term financing overhang — backlog now covers ~15x current annual revenue and the Anthropic loan facility (see prior Rockdale reporting) reprices existing debt cheaper, (2) confirms the AI-neocloud tenancy pool is deeper than hyperscalers alone (Jane Street enterprise-first LP-heavy commit), (3) 158% Q3 growth guide de-risks the FY26 street model, (4) $30B capex validates NVDA/VRT/ETN datacenter-power orderbook cadence.

headline: Samsung / SK Hynix rally 7-8%, KOSPI +4-5% intraday on Asia Business Daily report Singapore's Temasek plans first-ever direct S. Korean equity investments — sovereign fund views AI-memory as undervalued despite 2026 rally
summary: Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) each rose more than 7% during Asia trade Aug 12 after Seoul-based Asia Business Daily reported that Singapore sovereign fund Temasek (~S$518B AUM as of March 2026) has decided to invest directly in both chipmakers and has been in contact with the Korean government on execution timing. The report specifies Temasek will use its in-house team rather than external asset managers — a structural signal that the fund views memory-DRAM/HBM as core, not tactical, exposure. KOSPI opened at 6,438 and ran to intraday high 6,590 (+4-5%); foreigners were net buyers of ₩1.2T (~$848M). Bloomberg confirmed the report with additional sourcing. Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK) also rose in sympathy pre-market. Read-through for tracked names: (1) marginal-buyer step-up for the memory complex right into MU fiscal-Q4 (Sep) and the seasonal HBM4 ramp for NVDA Vera Rubin, (2) potential precursor to Korean government pushing shareholder-return acceleration at both names to defend the rally, (3) validates the Temasek-style institutional case that HBM/DDR5 pricing power extends through 2027 rather than peaking mid-2026 as some sell-side desks had modeled.

headline: July CPI cools: headline 3.4% Y/Y (from 3.5%) / +0.1% M/M, core 2.5% Y/Y — meets bar for Fed September hold; futures firm, Nasdaq +0.7% pre-mkt on relief plus SMCI/CRWV prints
summary: US July CPI released 8:30 AM ET Aug 12: headline +0.1% M/M and 3.4% Y/Y (down 0.1pp from June 3.5%), core +0.2% M/M and 2.5% Y/Y (down 0.1pp). The print landed in-line to slightly cooler on the Y/Y basis and materially cooler on the sequential composition — services ex-shelter continued to normalize. Read for the AI-infra complex: (1) reinforces the September Fed hold consensus and keeps the rate-cut path plausible for Q4 — supportive of long-duration high-multiple names (PLTR, CRWV, SMCI, memory), (2) removes the tail risk that a hot print revives the September hike case that Kevin Warsh had been floating publicly, (3) macro relief combines with two blockbuster AI-infra prints (SMCI, CRWV) — Nasdaq futures +0.7%, S&P +0.3%, Dow flat as we open pre-mkt. Semi complex leading: MU +3%, NVDA +2%, AMD +1%, INTC +2%, SMCI +9.5% (later reports show +23% intraday). No change to the underlying view that datacenter/power demand is macro-inelastic, but valuation dispersion narrows on lower discount rates.

headline: AI-infra complex rips pre-market on twin SMCI+CRWV beats: MU +3%, NVDA +2%, INTC +2%, AMD +1%, SMCI +9-23% intraday; hyperscaler capex trajectory now visibly bracketed for FY27
summary: Combined signal from SMCI's Q4 (record backlog, $60B new orders in a single quarter, FY27 rev guide as high as $72B) and CRWV's Q2 ($104B backlog excluding Q3's $25B+, $30B 2026 capex, 158% Q3 revenue growth guide) established two fresh anchor points on the FY27 hyperscaler capex distribution: Meta's Q2 contract expansion at CRWV ($21B through 2032) plus Anthropic's multi-workstream diversification implies the CY26 hyperscaler capex pool is more likely to surprise up than down. Reactions across our tracked complex during pre-market Aug 12: MU +3%, NVDA +2%, AMD +1%, INTC +2%, SMCI +9.5% (later reports +23% at peak). Read-through: (1) NVDA into Aug 26 earnings — SMCI's shipment guide implies GB200/GB300 platform demand is not seeing pause-for-Rubin, (2) MU into fiscal Q4 (Sep) — Temasek report + AI-infra print combo is a near-term momentum trifecta on HBM cycle, (3) VRT/ETN/GEV backlog implication is straightforwardly positive — $30B CRWV capex alone drops meaningful volume through the datacenter-electrical stack.
